Sensitivity Analysis for Sample Size Planning From the AIPE Perspective for a Mixed-Effects Fixed Effect

Source: R/ss_aipe_mixed_effects_sensitivity.R
ss_aipe_mixed_effects_sensitivity.Rd

Simulates the design that ss_aipe_mixed_effects plans and reports what its confidence interval for the fixed-effect slope delivers: the mean width, the share of intervals no wider than desired, and the coverage. The two functions take the same description of the predictor (predictor_level, centering, the intraclass correlation of the predictor), use the same expressions, and form the same interval, so a plan made by the first can be checked by the second, at the planning values or at population values that differ from them.

On each replication the function draws n_clusters clusters (i.e., Level 2 units) of cluster_size individuals (i.e., Level 1 units) from $$y_{ki} = \beta x_{ki} + u_k + e_{ki},$$ with \(u_k \sim N(0, \rho V)\) and \(e_{ki} \sim N(0, (1 - \rho) V)\), where \(\beta\) is true_reg_coef, \(V\) is true_total_var, and \(\rho\) is true_icc. An individual-level (i.e., Level 1) predictor is \(x_{ki} = b_k + w_{ki}\), with variance \(\rho_X \sigma^2_X\) between clusters and \((1 - \rho_X)\sigma^2_X\) within them (true_var_X, true_icc_X); a cluster-level (i.e., Level 2) predictor is \(x_k \sim N(0, \sigma^2_X)\), the same for every individual of a cluster. The predictor is then centered as centering says, the model is fit, and the interval \(\hat\beta \pm t_{1 - \alpha/2,\, \nu}\,\widehat{SE}(\hat\beta)\) is recorded, with the degrees of freedom \(\nu\) of ss_aipe_mixed_effects.

Usage

ss_aipe_mixed_effects_sensitivity(
  true_total_var = NULL,
  true_var_X = NULL,
  true_icc = NULL,
  true_reg_coef = 0,
  supposed_total_var = NULL,
  supposed_var_X = NULL,
  supposed_icc = NULL,
  width,
  cluster_size = 20L,
  specified_n_clusters = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  predictor_level = 1,
  centering = c("cluster_mean", "grand_mean", "none"),
  true_icc_X = 0,
  supposed_icc_X = true_icc_X,
  G = 1000,
  print_iter = FALSE,
  filename = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

true_total_var

Population variance of the outcome given the predictor, the variance of the random intercept plus the residual variance: the value the data are generated from.

true_var_X

Population variance of the predictor the data are generated from: over individuals for an individual-level predictor (between and within clusters together), over clusters for a cluster-level predictor.

true_icc

Population intraclass correlation of the outcome given the predictor (the share of true_total_var between clusters).

true_reg_coef

Population value of the fixed-effect slope, the regression coefficient of the outcome on the predictor (\(\beta\) in the model above; default 0). The width of the interval does not depend on it; the coverage is evaluated against it.

supposed_total_var, supposed_var_X, supposed_icc

Supposed values, the planning values passed to ss_aipe_mixed_effects (not estimates computed from data), which may differ from the population values above; supply all three, or specified_n_clusters, but not both.

width

Desired full width of the confidence interval for the slope.

cluster_size

Number of individuals in each cluster (the same in every cluster).

specified_n_clusters

Number of clusters to evaluate, in place of the number the planning values give.

conf_level

Confidence level (default 0.95).

predictor_level, centering

The level of the predictor (1, the default, or 2) and how it is centered ("cluster_mean", "grand_mean", or "none"), as in ss_aipe_mixed_effects. The same values are used to plan and to analyze each simulated data set.

true_icc_X

Population intraclass correlation of an individual-level predictor: the share of true_var_X between clusters in the data generated. Default 0. Not used with predictor_level = 2.

supposed_icc_X

The supposed value of true_icc_X, the planning value passed to ss_aipe_mixed_effects. Default: true_icc_X.

G

Number of Monte Carlo replications.

print_iter

Logical.

filename

Optional path for a comma separated file recording every replication (the fixed effect estimate, the two confidence limits, the interval width, and two indicators of whether the interval missed true_reg_coef below or above): nothing is written when filename is NULL (the default), a new file with a header row is created otherwise, an existing file at that path is appended to, and a throwaway run should point it at tempfile(fileext = ".csv").

seed

NULL (the default) to draw from the current random number stream, or a single number that makes the call reproducible; a supplied seed is set for this call only, and the caller's random number state is restored when the function returns.

Value

A data.frame with rows for the mean, median, and standard deviation of the estimated slope (mean_reg_coef, median_reg_coef, sd_reg_coef) and of the interval width, the share of intervals no wider than width (pct_ci_less_width), the shares that missed true_reg_coef below and above and their sum, the design simulated (n_clusters, cluster_size, total_N, predictor_level), the expected_width that ss_aipe_mixed_effects gives for that design at the population values, and the inputs. The centering is recorded in attr(x, "centering").

Details

How each case is fit. Two of the three analyses have closed forms in a balanced design and are computed directly. The slope of an individual-level predictor centered at its cluster mean is the within-cluster regression slope, with the residual mean square on \(K(m - 1) - 1\) degrees of freedom. The slope of a cluster-level predictor is the slope of the regression of the \(K\) cluster means of the outcome on the predictor, on \(K - 2\) degrees of freedom. In both, restricted maximum likelihood for the random-intercept model gives the same estimate and standard error when its estimate of the intercept variance is positive. An individual-level predictor that is centered at its grand mean or not centered has no closed form, because its weights depend on the estimated variance components; it is fit by restricted maximum likelihood with lme4, which must then be installed, and its interval uses \(K(m - 1) - 1\) degrees of freedom.

What to look at. mean_ci_width against width says whether the plan delivers the width on average, and pct_ci_less_width how often. total_type_I_error against \(1 - \) conf_level says whether the interval covers as it should; with few clusters and a cluster-level predictor this is where a problem would show. Replications in which no interval could be formed are counted in the record of the simulation.

The record of the simulation

Every sensitivity function of the package summarizes its replications over one denominator: the replications that produced a confidence interval (for a power sensitivity function, a test). The proportion of intervals that met the width target (pct_ci_less_width), the proportions of intervals that missed the true value, and the summaries of the widths are all taken over those replications. A replication without an interval is in none of these rows. It is counted, and the returned table carries the counts in its attribute simulation, a list read with attr(x, "simulation"):

attempted

the number of replications asked for (G).

returned

the number that produced an interval (a test).

failed

the number that did not (attempted - returned).

denominator

the number of replications the rows named above are taken over, which is returned.

width_target_probability

the proportion of the replications with an interval whose interval met the width target, the value of the pct_ci_less_width row; NA for a function or a call without a width target, and when no replication produced an interval.

width_target_mc_ci

the exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) limits for that proportion, at the confidence level of the table. They describe the error of the simulation, which shrinks as G grows, and nothing else.

A function that records more about its run adds elements to the list, and its help page names them. The line "Replications" beneath the printed table gives G, and the three counts when a replication was without an interval. With many replications without an interval the rows describe only the studies in which the interval could be formed, so failed is to be reported beside them.

References

McNeish, D., & Kelley, K. (2019). Fixed effects versus mixed effects models for clustered data: Reviewing the approaches, disentangling the differences, and making recommendations. Psychological Methods, 24, 20–35. doi:10.1037/met0000182

Maxwell, S. E., Delaney, H. D., & Kelley, K. (2027). Designing experiments and analyzing data: A model comparison perspective (4th ed.). Routledge. (See Chapters 15 and 16 on mixed-effects models.)

See also

ss_aipe_mixed_effects, icc_lmer

design_consequences for what a chosen design delivers: power, the Type S (sign) and Type M (exaggeration) errors of the significance filter, and the expected confidence interval width.

Examples

# Plan, then check the plan (few replications, for a fast example).
ss_aipe_mixed_effects(true_total_var = 1, true_var_X = 1, true_icc = 0.10,
                      width = 0.40, cluster_size = 10)
#>  term                 value
#>  necessary_n_clusters 10   
#>  total_N              100  
#>  width                0.400
#>  expected_width       0.400
#>  df                   89   
#>  true_icc             0.100
#>  true_icc_X           0    
#>  cluster_size         10   
#>  predictor_level      1    
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%
ss_aipe_mixed_effects_sensitivity(
  true_total_var = 1, true_var_X = 1, true_icc = 0.10,
  true_reg_coef = 0.30,
  supposed_total_var = 1, supposed_var_X = 1, supposed_icc = 0.10,
  width = 0.40, cluster_size = 10,
  G = 50, print_iter = FALSE, seed = 113
)
#>  term               value
#>  mean_reg_coef      0.311
#>  median_reg_coef    0.313
#>  sd_reg_coef        0.112
#>  mean_ci_width      0.398
#>  median_ci_width    0.393
#>  sd_ci_width        0.039
#>  pct_ci_less_width  0.560
#>  pct_ci_miss_low    0.020
#>  pct_ci_miss_high   0.020
#>  total_type_I_error 0.040
#>  n_clusters         10   
#>  cluster_size       10   
#>  total_N            100  
#>  predictor_level    1    
#>  expected_width     0.400
#>  true_total_var     1    
#>  true_var_X         1    
#>  true_icc           0.100
#>  true_icc_X         0

#>  conf_level         0.950
#> 
#> Replications: 50
#> 
#> Confidence level: 95%

# A cluster-level predictor, at a number of clusters chosen by hand.
ss_aipe_mixed_effects_sensitivity(
  true_total_var = 1, true_var_X = 1, true_icc = 0.10,
  true_reg_coef = 0.30,
  specified_n_clusters = 25, cluster_size = 10, width = 0.40,
  predictor_level = 2, centering = "grand_mean",

)
